ticket.subject: Print Spooler service terminates automatically on print server PRINT-CORP-01
ticket.raw_subject: Print Spooler service terminates automatically on print server PRINT-CORP-01
ticket.description: Multiple branch office users report unable to print to shared network printer 'HQ-FLOOR3-COLOR'. When investigating print server PRINT-CORP-01.synthetic-test.local (IP 192.0.2.15), the Print Spooler service (spoolsv.exe) is in a Stopped state. Manual attempts to start the service succeed for approximately 5 minutes before stopping again.

comments.body:
Connected to PRINT-CORP-01 via administrative session. Inspected Windows Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Application.
Found Event ID 1000, Application Error:
Faulting application name: spoolsv.exe, version: 10.0.20348.1907
Faulting module name: hpz3r500.dll, version: 0.3.1537.404
Exception code: 0xc0000005 (Access Violation)
Fault offset: 0x00000000000491a2

The crash correlates exactly with a large PDF print job submitted with complex vector gradients.

Remediation executed:
1. Stopped spooler service and flushed corrupted print job spool files:
   Stop-Service -Name Spooler -Force
   Remove-Item -Path 'C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS\*.*' -Force
2. Identified printer queue 'HQ-FLOOR3-COLOR' was using legacy Version 3 OEM driver 'HP Color LaserJet Enterprise M553 PCL6'.
3. Replaced driver with modern Type-4 Class Driver 'Microsoft Enhanced Point and Print Compatibility Driver'.
4. Removed offending driver package using pnputil:
   pnputil /delete-driver oem44.inf /uninstall /force
5. Started Print Spooler service:
   Start-Service -Name Spooler
6. Sent test calibration page and 50-page complex PDF document. Print Spooler remained stable and memory usage stayed under 45 MB.
